name: bind_expansion_drivers

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:c/Binddrivers:2:01E6
name: find_driver_entry

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:c/Binddrivers:2:021C
name: process_delimited_string_segments

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:c/Binddrivers:2:0268
name: split_slash_separated_part

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:c/Binddrivers:2:034A

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:c/Binddrivers:2:0368
name: check_nondigit_within_length
description: Scans characters up to a given length, skipping decimal digit characters, and returns one as soon as a non-digit is reached. It returns zero if the length runs out while the characters are still digits, and returns one at once when the length is zero.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:c/Binddrivers:2:0396
name: parse_decimal_integer
description: Reads characters from a null-terminated string and accumulates consecutive decimal digits into a number, stopping at the first character that is not a digit or at the terminator. It returns the accumulated value.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:c/Binddrivers:2:03C6

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:c/Binddrivers:4:0006
name: compare_two_strings

name: measure_string_length

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:c/Binddrivers:4:0024
name: measure_string_length
description: Returns the number of bytes before the zero terminator of the string addressed by the address register, using the same 16-bit counting as the stack-argument version.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:c/Binddrivers:4:0030
name: find_char_in_string
description: Scans a zero-terminated string for a given character and returns a pointer to its first occurrence, or null when the terminator is reached first.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:c/Binddrivers:4:004C
name: copy_c_string
description: Copies a zero-terminated string from the source address to the destination address, including the terminating zero byte.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:c/Binddrivers:4:0058
name: compute_range_adjusted_offset
description: Calls two routines to obtain a value and a range, returns zero when the range start is above its end or a further check fails, and otherwise returns the first value adjusted by the argument and the range start.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:c/EndCLI:0:0136
name: copy_table_block_to_buffer
description: Copies sixteen consecutive 32-bit words from a fixed table in the base register into the buffer pointer passed on the stack, when that pointer is not null. It then calls a routine through the exit vector.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:0:0000
name: clear_memory_and_launch_process
description: Clears a large block of memory and then sets up a new process: it builds a quoted command line from the argument text, copies a code block into the new process record and links that record into the process list. It releases the Forbid lock and returns after the launch call.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:0:0238
name: release_current_task_resources

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:0:02AE
name: shutdown_and_reply_message

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:0:030A

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:0:0322
name: call_two_table_entries

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:0:0334

name: decompress_lzss_stream

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:22:00D4
name: reverse_bits_in_words

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:22:0100
name: dispatch_request_by_code

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:22:01CC
name: swap_first_and_third_words

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:22:01E8

name: call_stored_library_routine

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:22:0272
name: stub_return_only
description: Returns immediately with no calls, memory access or hardware register use.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:22:0274
name: lookup_and_forward_request
description: Looks up a descriptor from the first argument and returns minus one if it is missing. Otherwise it seeks to the end of the stream when a flag bit is set, forwards the request with the remaining arguments and returns its result, or minus one when a global error flag is set.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:22:02DC
name: parse_printf_format_specifier
description: Parses a printf-style conversion specifier: it reads flags, width, precision and length modifiers, takes the next argument from the argument list for each conversion, and formats it as a character, decimal, hexadecimal, string or padded number. It writes the padding and digits through a character callback.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:22:0694
name: expand_format_string_with_callback
description: Walks a format string and passes each ordinary character to an output callback. Each percent conversion is handed to the specifier parser, and a doubled percent sign is output as a single one.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:22:06EC
name: allocate_stream_buffer_if_needed
description: Allocates a stream buffer when none is set up or a reset flag is present, storing the buffer pointers and clearing the counters. When allocation fails it records an error code and returns minus one; otherwise it returns zero.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:22:0748
name: write_char_with_newline_translation
description: Writes one character into a buffered stream, expanding each line feed into a carriage return followed by a line feed. It flushes the buffer through a lower-level write call when it is full or at the end, and records error and end flags in the stream state.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:22:09D8
name: read_buffered_character_with_eof
description: Reads one byte from a buffered stream, refilling the buffer through a lower-level read call when it is empty. It skips a carriage return before a line feed, sets an end flag on the end-of-file marker and returns minus one at end or on error.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:22:0B4C
name: process_flagged_table_entries
description: Walks a table of eight-byte entries from last to first, calling a routine with the stored value of each entry whose flag byte is set and whose bit four is clear. It then calls a final routine with its argument.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:22:0BA0
name: stub_jump_to_fixed_target

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:22:0BB4
name: read_uppercase_character
description: Calls two routines to obtain a byte, then converts it to uppercase when it is a lowercase letter and returns the result.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:22:0BD0
name: convert_lowercase_to_uppercase
description: Converts a lowercase ASCII letter to its uppercase form by subtracting the case offset, and returns any other character unchanged.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:22:0BE8
name: convert_uppercase_to_lowercase
description: Converts an uppercase ASCII letter to lowercase by adding the case offset, and returns any other character unchanged.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:22:0C00
name: tokenize_command_line_arguments
description: Splits a command line into up to thirty-two arguments on spaces, tabs and newlines, treating double-quoted text as a single argument and terminating each argument with a zero byte. It reports an error when a quote is left open, then passes the count and the argument list to a routine, using a default list when no arguments were found.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:22:0CBC
name: emit_characters_until_zero
description: When enough stack space is available, it repeatedly passes characters from a routine to two output routines until that routine returns a zero character, then returns the result of a final routine. Otherwise it reads a character through a routine and converts it to uppercase.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:22:0CC8
name: uppercase_string_in_place
description: Converts each character of a zero-terminated string to uppercase in place, changing only the characters that a lookup table in the base area flags as lowercase, and returns the string pointer.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:22:0D0C
name: copy_bounded_string_padded

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:22:0D30
name: measure_string_length
description: Returns the number of bytes before the zero terminator of the string it is given.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:22:0D44
name: copy_c_string
description: Copies a zero-terminated string from the source address to the destination address, including the terminating zero byte, and returns the destination pointer.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:22:0D54
name: compare_two_strings
description: Compares two zero-terminated strings character by character, returning a negative value when the first differing character is smaller or equal, a positive value when it is larger, and zero when the strings match up to the terminator.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:22:0D74
name: append_c_string
description: Appends a zero-terminated source string to the end of the destination string, including its terminator, and returns the destination pointer.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:22:0D8C
name: format_number_as_decimal_string
description: Converts a number into decimal digit characters by repeatedly calling a routine that yields each digit, stores them in a temporary buffer and copies them in reverse order to the output with a zero terminator. It returns the number of digits written.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:22:0DBC
name: convert_number_to_octal_string
description: Converts an unsigned number into octal digit characters, taking three bits at a time, and copies them in reverse order into the buffer with a zero terminator. It returns the number of digits written.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:22:0DFC
name: convert_number_to_hex_string
description: Converts an unsigned number into lowercase hexadecimal digit characters by taking one nibble at a time from a digit table, copies them in reverse order into the buffer with a zero terminator, and returns the digit count.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:22:0E28
name: parse_signed_decimal
description: Reads an optional plus or minus sign followed by decimal digits, stores the signed value through the integer pointer and returns the number of characters consumed.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:22:0E74
name: append_byte_to_buffer
description: Stores one byte at the current position of a global output buffer, advances the position and increments the byte count.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:22:0E8E
name: format_text_into_buffer

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:22:11D0
name: copy_memory_block
description: Copies a block of bytes from the source address to the destination address, copying backwards when the source is at or below the destination so that overlapping regions are handled correctly.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:22:11F8
name: fill_memory_with_byte
description: Writes the given byte value into each position of a block of the given length and returns the block start.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:22:1214

description: Looks up a descriptor from the first argument and returns minus one if it is missing. Otherwise it forwards the request with the remaining arguments and returns its result, or minus one when a global error flag is set.

name: read_items_from_stream
description: Reads a number of items of a given size from a stream structure into the destination buffer one byte at a time, and returns the count of complete items read before the stream ends or fails.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:22:15C4

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:22:1794

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:8:19E2
name: store_argument_in_global

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:8:19F4
name: divide_signed_32bit_values
description: Divides one signed 32-bit value by another by working on operand magnitudes and calling the unsigned division routine, then negates the result when the dividend is negative. It returns the 32-bit result.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:8:19FA
name: rebuild_buffers_by_stage
description: When enough stack space is available, it handles a stage code from zero to five by releasing and reallocating stored buffers, with each stage falling through to the next. It then calls a routine with one for any nonzero stage and returns the stage's stored table value.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:8:1A12
name: free_buffers_and_structures

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:8:1A1E

name: begin_nested_session
description: When enough stack space is available, it increments a session counter. On the first entry it obtains a stored handle through a routine and, when a flag is set, issues a further configuration call with fixed values. It returns the counter value from before the increment.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:8:1A3C
name: store_adjusted_masked_value

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:8:1A54
name: call_global_routine_after_argument

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:8:1A6C

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:8:1A72
name: end_nested_session
description: When enough stack space is available, it decrements the session counter. When the counter reaches zero it calls a routine with a fixed value and, when a flag is set, issues a further call with fixed arguments. It returns the register value.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:8:1A78
name: release_nonzero_slots
description: When enough stack space is available, it visits four slots and, for each one that is set, stores a value, issues a routine call with the value eighty, writes a field of a stored structure and clears the slot. It returns sixteen.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:8:1A84
name: send_buffer_entry
description: When enough stack space is available, it selects one of two stored buffers by the first argument. When the second argument is set, it passes the buffer, a pointer read just before that argument and the value stored there to a routine, returning its result, otherwise zero.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:8:1A8A
name: select_and_call_by_result
description: When enough stack space is available, it calls a routine with its argument. When the result is nonzero it calls a routine with two fixed table addresses, otherwise it calls a routine with no arguments, and it returns that result.

name: multiply_fixed_point_values
description: Multiplies two 32-bit values held in the data and address registers by combining their high and low 16-bit halves in cross-term products, and returns the 32-bit result.

name: measure_text_without_trailing_spaces

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:20:0036
name: wait_for_key_with_cycling_marker
description: When enough stack space is available, it loops until a key is read. Each pass writes a fixed set of control and space codes and one character from a four-entry table that advances each time, then pauses before the next pass. The escape code is passed to a routine when the loop ends.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:20:00D6
name: read_char_in_range
description: When enough stack space is available, it reads characters through a routine until one falls within the range given by the two arguments or the escape code is read, and returns that character.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:20:0114
name: wait_until_value_received
description: When enough stack space is available, it repeatedly calls a routine until it returns the argument value. When the argument is odd it calls a further routine, and it returns the final result.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:20:0138
name: read_char_in_range_or_return
description: When enough stack space is available, it reads characters until one falls within the given range or the return or escape code is read, and stores each character read. It returns the last character.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:20:017C
name: call_fixed_table_routine
description: When enough stack space is available it returns the result of a routine called with a fixed table address. Otherwise it reads a byte through two routines and returns it converted to uppercase when it is a lowercase letter.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:20:0190
name: poll_routine_with_retries
description: When enough stack space is available, it calls a routine up to twice the argument number of times, stopping as soon as it returns a nonzero value. Each failed attempt calls a fallback routine with the value five, and the last result is returned.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:20:01BA
name: poll_until_nonzero_register
description: Repeatedly calls a routine and calls a fallback with the value five after each failed attempt, returning the data register value once a nonzero result is obtained.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:20:01CC
name: call_routine_by_threshold
description: When enough stack space is available, it calls a routine with the argument, the value one and the value thirty-two. When the argument exceeds 999 it first adjusts it through a routine and afterwards calls a routine with seventy-five. It returns the final result.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:20:0224
name: copy_state_and_call_routines
description: When enough stack space is available, it copies several state bytes into a saved area, points a stored pointer at a buffer and calls a series of routines with the state and two fixed sizes. It then restores the saved pointer and returns the result of the final call.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:20:02C4
name: visit_neighbour_positions
description: When enough stack space is available, it visits a five-by-three set of positions around a stored position, wrapping the coordinates at sixty-four. For each position it calls routines with the stored values, and it returns minus three.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:20:03F8
name: set_three_entry_values
description: When enough stack space is available, it calls a routine three times with successive indices, passing a value from a stored table each time, then returns twenty-three.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:20:0438
name: reset_five_stored_entries
description: When enough stack space is available, it releases each non-null entry of a five-entry table through a routine and clears it. It then fills the table again from entries selected by stored bytes below a limit, and returns five.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:20:04E2
name: compare_stored_value_with_result
description: When enough stack space is available, it calls a routine and returns one when a stored 16-bit value is below its result, otherwise zero.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:20:0524
name: lookup_flag_in_table_rows
description: Looks up table entries for a byte argument and for five stored bytes. It returns one when a matching entry has the code two, zero when a matching entry is empty, and two otherwise.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:20:05B8
name: reacquire_indexed_resource
description: When enough stack space is available, it releases a previously stored resource if one is held, then obtains a new one from a table indexed by a stored byte and stores it. It returns the resource, or the index byte itself when the index is seventeen or more.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:20:05FA
name: layout_gadget_panel
description: When enough stack space is available, it removes a gadget, sets up display rows from stored tables and draws the entries in two groups depending on a flag. It finishes with a final call and returns its result.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:20:078A
name: update_entry_for_mode
description: When enough stack space is available and a stored mode byte is not one, it passes a stored value and two table entries to routines and returns the result of a further call. Otherwise it returns zero.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:20:0818
name: apply_default_configuration
description: When enough stack space is available, it clears a stored byte, issues a series of configuration calls with stored values and fixed numbers, and returns the result of a final call.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:20:088E
name: build_interface_and_wait_for_input
description: When enough stack space is available, it removes an existing gadget list if one is present, builds gadgets and text items from fixed coordinates and stored tables, then loops reading input until a nonzero code arrives. It finishes with a final call and returns its result.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:20:0BA8
name: run_input_loop_until_escape
description: When enough stack space is available, it releases stored resources, clears a status table and rebuilds a lookup table from stored values. It then loops reading keys until the escape code arrives, drawing entries chosen from the tables on each pass.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:20:106E
name: refresh_gadget_states
description: When enough stack space is available, it sets up a refresh with a fixed call. For each of eight stored flags that is clear it calls a routine with the index, and it repeats the same for seventeen further entries offset by eight. It returns the result of a final call.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:20:1110
name: draw_entry_frame
description: When enough stack space is available, it draws a frame around one of the stored entries by issuing a series of move and line calls with coordinates taken from tables, then returns the result of the final call.

key: king's bounty (1990)(new world computing)[cr csl][a3]/King's Bounty (1990)(New World Computing)[cr CSL][a3].adf:King's Bounty:20:124C
name: reset_state_and_call_routine
